sentences.text: Placochelys resembled a sea turtle, reaching a length of about 90 cm with a flat, turtle-like shell covered in knobby plates and a compact triangular skull.
Researchers suggest the specialized broad teeth on Placochelys's palate were used for crushing shellfish and hard-shelled prey.
It had paddle-shaped limbs for swimming with discernable toes and a short tail, unlike modern sea turtles.
Fossils of Placochelys have been found in Germany, Austria, Hungary, and Italy.
Placochelys belongs to the superorder Sauropterygia, order Placodontia, and family Placochelyida, and it is classified as a reptile.
Placochelys fossils date to the Late Triassic, specifically from the Norian to Rhaetian stages, living between 221.5 and 205.6 million years ago.
The animal lived in the Middle and Late Triassic in what is now Germany.
